posts.name: Phantom5613
posts.cooked:
Breaking a rule by answering yesterday's question, but I figure I have a bit of say in the matter since I actually work at a library. I don't think physical libraries will be phased out any time soon, but like what Dandolo suggested, they need to adapt and change with the times to stay relevent to the modern day.

For example, my branch(of the 21 in our county that do the same) doesn't exclusivly carry only physical, regular format books.  We've got a section of Large print books for the elderly and visualy impared. We cary books on CD which are very popular with old folks who can't read normal text as well as they used to OR for folks who spend a lot of their time commuting from work and want to fill the void with something. Playaways(Imagine a small MP3 player that holds a single audiobook that takes a single AAA battery) are also good for that group, just don't listen to it while your driving. We have a massive collection of DVDs and Blurays with movies ranging from black and white classics to the newest releases, not to mention the ammount of television series and Non-fiction documentaries and foreign films. Our music collection is pretty impressive. We have patrons who come in everyday to use our public-use computers, and the kids and young adult sections are almost mini-libraries of their own. I haven't even mentioned the numerous gatherings and day-events we hold year-round.

And yes, we carry a large collection of digital books that we can loan out from our online services.

So no, I don't think physical libraries will be phased out soon. They need to change with the needs of the public they serve to stay relevent. If they can do that, then I think brick and mortar libraries should be around for a good while still.

As for the current question: I haven't had the chance to travel outside the country as of yet. Not that I don't want to, the chance just hasn't shown itself yet. The farthest I've traveled is I want to say Florida.

I've listened to a couple audiobooks. One of my favorites hands-down is 'The Hobbit'. There's a number of songs and such in there, and it's nice to get a reminder of how the classic book went.
